title: Adaptive Semantic Gates for Reliable Multi-Agent LLMs
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: The ASG evaluates a candidate action given the current contextual state by estimating a semantic hazard score... Actions whose risk exceeds an adaptive threshold are blocked, attenuated, or returned for revision... In Notes, it blocks full-workspace resets... In Todo Manager, it intercepts cascading deletions... In workflow environments, ASG halts high-severity tool calls including session resets, buffer wipes, and dataset overwrites.
rationale: No adversary: hazards come from coordination breakdowns, noisy states and cascading errors; 'adversarial' stress events are destructive actions, not attacks.

title: Automated Interpretation of Fleet Incidents to Enable System Level Runtime Assurance
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Insufficiencies of the validation and assumptions taken at design time necessitate mechanisms to handle violations at runtime... High-Priority Safety Goal: Count of occurrences where the vehicle comes within 1 meter of a VRU at speeds greater than 20 km/h and endangers VRUs... Following the execution of the assurance framework process to validate the assumptions and track additional domain information.
rationale: Runtime safety assurance for vehicle fleets; violations stem from operational and design insufficiencies, no adversary.

title: Agentic AI Security: Threats, Defenses, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
evidence_excerpt: ADV: AI Prompt injection (PI) remains the most widely discussed attack in the literature, where malicious instructions cause the model to deviate from intended behavior... Beyond traditional text-based prompt injection, AI agents are increasingly vulnerable to attacks that exploit the growing capabilities of modern models... Multi-agent ecosystems amplify risk through protocol-mediated interactions. Message tampering, role spoofing, and protocol exploitation create opportunities for adversaries to compromise not only a single agent but entire coordinated workflows.
rationale: Survey organized around deliberate attacks (injection, jailbreaks, protocol attacks); fault tolerance only mentioned in passing.

title: COSTAR: Cloud-Observed Safety and Trust-Aware Agentic Reasoning for Enterprise Workflows
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: The system identifies hallucination-sensitive claims and requires evidence binding to ensure factual grounding of generated content... The controller computes expected-utility scores incorporating penalties for policy violations, uncertainty levels, and resource consumption... Actions exceeding established risk thresholds are automatically rejected or undergo revision processes.
rationale: Policy violations, hallucination and runaway cost from model errors; adversarial red-teaming is future work only.

title: Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Framework for Robust Prompt Injection Defense in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
evidence_excerpt: ADV: This paper will present a Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Defense Framework that will sanitize any user- or agent-generated prompts and validate the output of the LLM independently... Cross-Agent Isolation: Malicious instructions cannot move across nodes... The suggested framework has a detection rate of 94%... higher than that of keyword filtering, post-hoc output filtering, safety fine-tuning, and SingleVLM.
rationale: Method and evaluation target multimodal prompt injection; no fault-based component.

title: A Distributed Multi-Agent Framework for Real-Time Privacy Monitoring and Compliance in Enterprise AI Systems
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Agent hallucinations may inadvertently generate outputs resembling real sensitive data. We model this risk through three detection mechanisms: ... Synthetic Data Similarity Scoring... Pattern Convergence Detection... Context Leakage Through Hallucination... Our system achieved 94.7% overall accuracy... detection of hallucination-based leakage invisible to traditional systems (91.7% vs. 0-5.2%). | ADV: Sophisticated privacy attacks extract information through seemingly innocent multi-turn conversations. We model conversations as directed graphs... Attack detection identifies paths through the graph that progressively reveal sensitive information... We tested 50,000 user interaction scenarios and 2,500 adversarial cases... Behavioral drift detection identified 12 emergent capabilities and 5 multi-turn attacks completely missed by baselines.
rationale: Both: hallucination-privacy risk detection (no adversary) and multi-turn extraction-attack detection, each with its own evaluation.

title: AgentGuard: Runtime Verification of AI Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Factors such as (1) stochasticity and unpredictability, (2) Hallucinations, (3) Emergent unintended behaviors and (4) susceptibility to new vulnerabilities, all contribute to this increased risk... our emphasis is on managing the unpredictability of these agentic systems and offering a roadmap to address the emergent behaviors of MASs based on our approach... AgentGuard learns its repair strategy's AMDP... Success probability predicts fix likelihood and guides resource allocation and interventions when low.
rationale: Scope explicitly limited to stochasticity and hallucination; attacks are mentioned only in the problem statement.

title: Explainable, Verifiable Agentic AI with Provably Reduced Failure Modes Using Quantum Verification Subroutines
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: These quantum modules serve as real-time safety checkers, ensuring that agent policies satisfy encoded constraints before execution... SafeGridSim: Power grid frequency control under load shifts and fault injection... When the quantum module is disabled, failure rates increased by 6.4% on average and explanation fidelity dropped by 18.7%.
rationale: Safety invariants against faults and instability, evaluated with fault injection; adversarial robustness is future work.

title: MCP-Secure: A Runtime Access Control Layer for Privilege-Aware LLM Agent Tooling
evidence_excerpt: ADV: To evaluate the robustness of MCP-Secure under adversarial pressure, we embed an attack simulation harness directly into the host-side mediation layer. This harness injects controlled adversarial variants of tool calls while preserving the agent's reasoning loop... Three classes of attacks are modeled. The first, Privilege Escalation... The second, Malicious Tool Metadata Injection... The third, Multi-Tool Confusion and Chaining
rationale: Explicit threat model (privilege escalation, tool-metadata injection); every run includes an attack, no non-adversarial condition is evaluated (cf. record 80).

title: ReSonAte: A Runtime Risk Assessment Framework for Autonomous Systems
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: This risk may arise due to distribution shifts, environmental context, or failure of software or hardware components... ReSonAte uses design-time BTD models along with information about the system's current state derived from system monitors (e.g. anomaly detectors, assurance monitors, etc.) and the operating environment (e.g. weather, traffic, etc.) to estimate dynamic hazard rates.
rationale: Dynamic risk estimation driven by component faults, sensor degradation and weather; no adversary.

title: Automating Prompt Leakage Attacks on Large Language Models Using Agentic Approach
evidence_excerpt: ADV: We define a prompt leakage-safe system as one in which an attacker cannot distinguish between two agents: one initialized with an original prompt and the other with a prompt stripped of all sensitive information... This work establishes a systematic methodology for adversarial testing of prompt leakage... A larger advantage indicates that the judge is better at distinguishing between responses from the sanitized and unsanitized prompts.
rationale: Formal security definition and probing framework for deliberate prompt-leakage attacks.

title: PRISM-AI: A Dual-Stage Neuro-Symbolic Agentic Framework for Privacy Risk Mitigation in LLMs
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Even without fine-tuning, LLMs may inadvertently process or expose sensitive information through user inputs or generated outputs, creating threats of personal data leakage, re-identification, and non-compliance with regulations... This stage ensures coverage of cases where sensitive information is inferred or hallucinated by the LLM.
rationale: Inadvertent privacy leakage during normal inference; adversarial testing is future work.

title: Agentic Moderation: Multi-Agent Design for Safer Vision-Language Models
evidence_excerpt: ADV: Malicious users can exploit cross-modal interactions and the continuous nature of visual embedding spaces... we design a concrete agentic moderation system for defending LVLMs against cross-modal adversarial attacks... our method reduces Attack Success Rate (ASR) by 7-19%... across five datasets [including AdvBench, FigStep, MM-Safety, SIUO] and four representative large vision-language models.
rationale: Framework and evaluation defend against cross-modal jailbreaks; no fault-based content.

title: ControlA: Agentic Workflow Control Mechanisms for Reliable Science
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: AI agents may need safeguards to prevent them from suggesting unsafe chemical reactions, misinterpreting experimental data, or following implausible reasoning pathways... [motivating example of GPT o1 producing wrong wildfire-risk grid values] Consequences: The presence of incorrect data... implies potential inaccuracies in assessing wildfire risk... IsVolumeSafe(A, 3, cl)? IsDosageSafe... verification steps help prevent the execution of ill-formed or hazardous actions. | ADV: Beyond unintentional errors, these systems are also susceptible to adversarial manipulation; malicious inputs or prompt injections can exploit vulnerabilities in LLMs, such as jailbreaking... we propose harmful-data tags... to trace the origin and propagation of harmful information, whether it arises from hallucinations, reasoning faults, or adversarial prompt injections, and to trigger targeted recovery actions.
rationale: Both: the containment and provenance mechanism is designed for hallucinations, reasoning faults and prompt injection alike.

title: Autonomous Agents in a Zero-Trust World: Architecting Secure, Auditable AI Workflows
evidence_excerpt: ADV: The adversary may: (1) craft malicious prompts or API responses to inject instructions, (2) poison training data or compromise model weights, (3) exploit vulnerabilities in the agent runtime to execute arbitrary code, or (4) attempt to exfiltrate data through covert channels... The SAW agent achieves a mean detection rate of 0.92... significantly higher than the baseline's 0.73 [for detecting adversarial actions].
rationale: Formal threat model and evaluation of malicious-action detection; no fault-based content.

title: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Governance and Security of LLM-Based Knowledge Access
evidence_excerpt: ADV: The 500 prompts included: (i) 250 malicious (prompt injection/jailbreak), (ii) 125 authorized, and (iii) 125 unauthorized-but-non-malicious... Threat models assumed (i) curious insiders with partial privileges attempting escalation, and (ii) malicious outsiders attempting jailbreaks... our system achieved 100%... The Router alone blocked 79.9%... LLM-only guardrails remain probabilistic and susceptible to jailbreaks.
rationale: Evaluation blocks injection and privilege escalation; 'unauthorized but non-malicious' is an access-control distinction, not a fault analysis.

title: PromptArmor: Simple yet Effective Prompt Injection Defenses
evidence_excerpt: ADV: In such attacks, an attacker embeds a malicious prompt–referred to as an injected prompt–into the data sample. As a result, the LLM executes the attacker-specified task instead of the intended user task... PromptArmor prompts an off-the-shelf LLM to detect and remove potential injected prompts from the input before the agent processes it.
rationale: Defense against prompt injection on AgentDojo, including adaptive attacks.

title: Guardrailing LLM and Agentic Decisions for 6G AI-RAN
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Common intrinsic limitations are: Lack of Knowledge—factual hallucinations from training data limitations; Lack of Computational Capability—poor mathematical, optimization, and logical reasoning... Agent-level solutions like RAG enable agents to dynamically fetch accurate, real-time information from external knowledge sources, reducing factual inaccuracies. | ADV: Common extrinsic threats are: Jailbreak Attacks—crafted prompts bypassing safety mechanisms; Backdoor Attacks—malicious training data implanting covert vulnerabilities; Prompt Injection—manipulation to leak sensitive information... Defending Against Jailbreak, Backdoor, and Injection Attacks LLM-level defenses include training with adversarial datasets and activation engineering. Agent-level protections incorporate input/output detectors, filters, and rewriters to intercept malicious prompts or responses.
rationale: Both: the review maps guardrails separately to intrinsic limitations (hallucination) and extrinsic attacks (jailbreak, injection).

title: [Short Paper] Forensic Analysis of Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: To mount IPI attacks, adversaries plant crafted malicious prompts that deceive LLMs into generating outputs designed to bypass intended agent functionality... We introduce a novel approach for forensic analysis of LLM agent execution logs to identify IPI attacks.
rationale: Forensic detection of indirect prompt-injection attacks in logs.

title: BladeRunner-AD: Adversarial Co-evolution of Robust and Interpretable Driving Policies via LLM Agent Games
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: The core idea of BladeRunner-AD is to model the optimization of a driving policy as a two-player, zero-sum game... The Defender generates a policy, which is then stress-tested by the Attacker in the simulator... this mechanism, akin to automated red teaming, forces the generated rules to be continuously refined, thereby achieving high robustness [against] complex traffic situations / unseen, malicious corner cases (i.e., hazardous driving scenarios, not a malicious actor attacking the AI system).
rationale: The 'attacker' agent generates worst-case traffic scenarios for robustness; no malicious actor targets the system.

title: Securing Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Threat Model and Mitigation Framework for Generative AI Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: T1: Reasoning Path Hijacking... Attackers manipulate the logical pathways that AI agents use for decision-making... T4: Unauthorized Action Execution... Attackers manipulate the agent to execute actions or use tools in ways that violate intended permissions.
rationale: All nine threats and mitigations are attacker-driven (STRIDE-based).

title: Toward Agentic and Self-Evolving Safety Evaluation of LLMs
evidence_excerpt: ADV: Adversarial Perturbation: To assess alignment robustness against deceptive user intent, the agent calls its function in jailbreak mode. This mode employs red-teaming techniques (e.g., persona-play, ethical dilemmas) to transform the base question into a jailbreak prompt... the Analyst agent... formulates a new attack strategy Sattack designed to exploit the identified weaknesses.
rationale: Self-evolving evaluation generates jailbreak strategies, compared against jailbreak baselines.

title: A Unified Framework for Safeguarding Multi-Agent Systems
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Hallucination (r1.6) measures the agent's tendency to fabricate false information, including non-existent references, incorrect facts, or fictitious tool outputs, particularly in contexts where the agent lacks sufficient knowledge and should instead acknowledge uncertainty... Cascading Failure (r3.1) occurs when a single-point failure, such as one agent producing erroneous output or becoming unresponsive, which triggers a chain reaction of failures across the system. | ADV: Prompt Injection (r1.1) targets the boundary between trusted instructions and untrusted user input: an adversary crafts input that causes the agent to override its system prompt or execute unintended instructions... Identity Spoofing (r2.6) tests whether an agent or external adversary can impersonate a trusted agent in the system.
rationale: Both: separate pass rates for non-adversarial risks (hallucination, cascading failure) and attacks (injection, jailbreak, poisoning, spoofing).

title: A Blockchain-Monitored Agentic AI Architecture for Trusted Perception–Reasoning–Action Pipelines
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Smart contracts effectively blocked 14 unsafe or unreasonable actions, which proves that blockchain validation can prevent high-impact autonomous actions that are not monitored... CheckSafetyBounds(Params, Policy) == False then EmitEvent("SafetyViolation", AgentID); return Rejection("SafetyBoundsExceeded").
rationale: Enforcement of safety bounds and policy compliance; the whitelist is generic access control, not tied to an attack.

title: MobiLLM: An Agentic AI Framework for Closed-Loop Threat Mitigation in 6G Open RANs
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Unlike human experts, LLMs can hallucinate—generating plausible but false information, which could lead to incorrect and potentially disruptive mitigation actions in a live network. Therefore, the design of MobiLLM focuses on implementing robust guardrails that ensure its trustworthiness and operational safety... This critical safety guardrail ensures the LLM can only provide parameters while the rigid script controls the execution logic (the how), preventing any unsafe or unintended operations. | ADV: Downlink IMSI Extraction Attack. A Downlink IMSI Extraction attack involves a man-in-the-middle attacker who intercepts and modifies a pre-authentication RRC message, forcing the UE to reveal its permanent identity (IMSI) in plain text... MobiLLM executed a successful, human-supervised remediation workflow [for a Null Cipher-Integrity attack caused by] a misconfigured base station.
rationale: Both: guardrails against the agent's own hallucination and misconfiguration, and mitigation of real network attacks.

title: SEVerA: Verified Synthesis of Self-Evolving Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: The absence of formal safety verification leads to failures across diverse domains. In program verification, agents cheat by subtly modifying the input program... In code repair, agents delete failing tests rather than fixing the underlying bugs... FGGM... wraps the underlying parametric generative model in a rejection sampler with a verified fallback... every returned output satisfies the specified contract for any input and any parameter setting of the underlying model.
rationale: Formal contracts and verified fallback against unreliable generative outputs; 'rogue agents' is background only.

title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM - Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: Large language model agents equipped with persistent memory are vulnerable to memory poisoning attacks, where adversaries inject malicious instructions through query only interactions that corrupt the agent's long term memory... Attackers: The attacker is a regular user with no elevated privileges... Attacker Goals: The attacker aims to induce malicious reasoning by the agent and persist malicious records in long-term memory.
rationale: Memory-poisoning attack replication and two defenses; explicit attacker throughout.

title: Zombie Agents: Persistent Control of Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Self-Reinforcing Injections
evidence_excerpt: ADV: We formalize a persistent attack we call a Zombie Agent, where an attacker covertly implants a payload that survives across sessions, effectively turning the agent into a puppet of the attacker... Attacker capabilities. We assume a strict black-box attacker... Attacker goals. The attacker aims to write a malicious payload Z into memory.
rationale: Indirect prompt injection leading to persistent memory compromise; attack-centric evaluation.

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
evidence_excerpt: ADV: MemoryGraft... is a novel indirect injection attack that compromises agent behavior not through immediate jailbreaks, but by implanting malicious successful experiences into the agent's long-term memory... The adversary Aadv is a malicious user who interacts with the agent only through legitimate input channels... The goal of the attacker Aadv is to induce a persistent behavioral drift in the agent.
rationale: Memory-poisoning attack and cryptographic-provenance defense.

title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-Based Agent Memory
evidence_excerpt: ADV: An adversary can inject seemingly harmless records into an agent's memory to manipulate its future behavior... The adversary aims to corrupt the agent's memory through a memory-poisoning attack, injecting a limited set of malicious records Madv into the agent's memory... We evaluated our framework against the sophisticated AgentPoison attack.
rationale: Defense against memory-poisoning attacks (AgentPoison, MINJA-style).

title: AgentLAB: Benchmarking LLM Agents against Long-Horizon Attacks
evidence_excerpt: ADV: LLM agents are increasingly deployed... but this expansion exposes them to long-horizon attacks that exploit multi-turn user-agent-environment interactions... we consider a red-teaming setting where the adversary aims to induce the agent to perform a malicious task T* (e.g., exfiltrate confidential data) through multi-round interactions.
rationale: Benchmark built around five adversarial attack families.

title: Enforcing Temporal Constraints for LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Example Scenario (benign, non-adversarial τ-bench task): 'One τ-bench test case involves a user, Sofia Li, who contacts the agent requesting to return a digital camera from her order #W8855135. When tested with DynaGuard... the agent immediately attempted to call get_order_details with the provided order ID without authenticating the user first, which violates the safety policy.' The method (Agent-C's SMT-based temporal constraint enforcement) is evaluated on the standard benign τ-bench benchmark (115 retail / 50 airline tasks) where non-conformance arises from ordinary agent reasoning failures about action sequencing, not from any adversary. | ADV: 'Benchmarks (adversarial). We extend both classes of scenarios in τ-Bench with adversarial benchmark instances, where a user attempts to accomplish a goal that is forbidden by the policy... Prior works also include strings in the prompts of the language model to elicit policy non-compliance... For a scenario, we assign the agent a Harm score of 1.0, if the agent generates the sequence of calls that are defined as malicious.' Results: 'In adversarial settings, Agent-C achieves 0% harm across all configurations, while unrestricted [baselines]... can be harmful under adversarial attack (up to 29.41% for Sonnet on retail).'
rationale: Both: the same enforcement is evaluated on benign ordering errors and on malicious users trying to force forbidden actions.

title: Removing the Big Red Button: Uncrewed Ground Vehicles in Complex Military Environments
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'We evaluate the hazards and associated risks associated with operating an optionally crewed vehicle, using a bow-tie diagram approach to define revised safety architectures for more automated motion termination.' The hazard analysis (FuHA, FMEA, bow-tie diagrams) targets 'unintentional movement or operation of the UGV', mechanical component malfunction, and environmental factors (e.g. GNSS jamming) as hazard triggers, addressed via preventive/reactive Motion Termination System barriers.
rationale: Hazard analysis of mechanical failure and safe motion termination; 'bad actors' appears only as motivation.

title: VirtualCrime: Evaluating Criminal Potential of Large Language Models via Sandbox Simulation
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'it remains largely underexplored what level of threat these models pose once an adversary successfully assigns them a malicious role... Following the framing of model evaluation for extreme risks, VirtualCrime is an elicitation setting... we explicitly assign the model a criminal identity and objective to bypass the initial "refusal" layer.' The framework measures multi-step criminal planning/execution (theft, kidnapping, sabotage, etc.) elicited after bypassing safety alignment/refusal, i.e. a jailbreak/misuse-style threat model.
rationale: Reconciled (Pass 3): assigning a criminal role to bypass refusals is a jailbreaking mechanism; no separate functional contribution.

title: When Refusals Fail: Unstable Safety Mechanisms in Long-Context LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: "We find that LLM agents could be sensitive to length, type, and placement of the context, exhibiting unexpected and inconsistent shifts in task performance and in refusals to execute harmful requests... Refusal rates shift unpredictably: GPT-4.1-nano increases from ~5% to ~40% while Grok 4 Fast decreases from ~80% to ~10% at 200K tokens."
rationale: Reconciled (Pass 3): context-length padding is an environmental variable, not a manipulation technique; the object is refusal instability.

title: Survival at Any Cost? LLMs and the Choice Between Self-Preservation and Human Harm
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'DECIDE-SIM... evaluates LLM agents in multi-agent survival scenarios where they must choose between ethically permissible resource... or tap into a human-critical resource that is explicitly forbidden.' Agents autonomously choose to harm humans (tapping a forbidden power grid that powers hospitals) due to self-preservation/resource-scarcity pressure, with no external adversary manipulating them; the proposed Ethical Self-Regulation System (ESRS) mitigates these unsafe autonomous actions via internal affective feedback.
rationale: Harm arises from the agent's own decisions under resource pressure; no manipulation.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'AgentSpec successfully prevents unsafe executions in over 90% of code agent cases, eliminates all hazardous actions in embodied agent tasks, and enforces 100% compliance by autonomous vehicles (AVs).' Evaluated risks are unintended/unsafe agent actions: risky code execution (vulnerability categories like path traversal, buggy regex), embodied-agent physical hazards (fire, electrical shock), and AV law violations -- none involving an external adversary manipulating the agent.
rationale: Evaluated hazards are destructive commands, physical hazards and traffic violations; adversarial manipulation concerns related work only.

title: Agent-SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Failure-mode taxonomy (Table 4) covering non-adversarial reasoning errors: 'The assistant ignores implicit or potential risks, and incorrectly calls tools (e.g., turning off all fire alarms ignoring the potential risks).' 'The assistant puts excessive trust in tool results without validation.' These behavioral risk categories (e.g. property loss, physical harm, compromised availability) arise from the agent's own lack of risk awareness/robustness, without any adversary instructing it to misbehave. | ADV: 'Note that for the category Produce unsafe information / misinformation, which does not involve tool usage, we sample 50 raw questions from AdvBench (Zou et al., 2023) and randomly combine them with 20 representative jailbreak templates (Zhang et al., 2024c), resulting in 200 new test cases.'
rationale: Both: benchmark construction includes non-adversarial failure modes and jailbreak/injection test categories.

title: Adaptive Attacks on Trusted Monitors Subvert AI Control Protocols
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'We instantiate a simple adaptive attack vector by which the attacker embeds publicly known or zero-shot prompt injections in the model outputs. Using this tactic, frontier models consistently evade diverse monitors and complete malicious tasks on two main AI control benchmarks.'
rationale: Untrusted model crafts prompt injections to subvert monitor-based control protocols.

title: Large Empirical Case Study: Go-Explore adapted for AI Red Team Testing
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'A prompt injection attack occurs when malicious instructions hidden in tool outputs (emails, files, web pages) override the agent's original task.' The paper adapts Go-Explore to systematically discover prompt injection attacks (e.g. PROMPT INJECTION WRITE, READ SECRET) against a safety-trained GPT-4o-mini agent, tracked via 'verified attack' criteria with causal injection chains.
rationale: Automated discovery of prompt injections (red-teaming).

title: Beyond Jailbreaking: Auditing Contextual Privacy in LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'How can adaptive adversary agents deliberately steer the conversation over multiple turns to induce privacy leakages?... adaptive multi-turn adversaries succeed where carefully engineered privacy jailbreak baselines fail, leaking protected attributes in up to 75% of conversations tested.' The CMPL framework models an adaptive LLM adversary that manipulates conversations via strategist/prompt-generator/predictor sub-modules to extract protected attributes.
rationale: Adaptive adversary agent manipulates conversations to extract private information.

title: DREAM: Dynamic Red-teaming across Environments for AI Models
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'sophisticated adversaries do not rely on a single malicious prompt, but instead orchestrate chains of seemingly benign interactions across disparate environments to bypass filters and achieve a critical breach... over 68% of long-chain exploits successfully bypass existing defenses.' DREAM models a persistent, adaptive adversary via a Cross-Environment Adversarial Knowledge Graph and Contextualized Guided Policy Search to synthesize multi-stage exploit chains.
rationale: Multi-stage adversarial red-teaming with attacker roles.

title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Model Safety Tiers
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'We present a stage-decomposed analysis of prompt injection attacks against five frontier LLM agents... instrument every run with a cryptographic canary token... tracked through four kill-chain stages—EXPOSED, PERSISTED, RELAYED, EXECUTED.'
rationale: Stage-level tracking of indirect prompt-injection attacks and defenses.

title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'we evaluate eight different defenses and bypass all of them using adaptive attacks, consistently achieving an attack success rate of over 50%. This reveals critical vulnerabilities in current defenses [against indirect prompt injection].'
rationale: Adaptive attacks against indirect prompt-injection defenses.

title: Who Tests the Testers? Systematic Enumeration and Coverage Audit of LLM Agent Tool Call Safety
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'we do not explicitly assume a malicious user: the scenarios we generate involve benign or ambiguous user intent, where harm arises from the agent's failure to reason about structural complexity in the environment rather than from adversarial manipulation.' SafeAudit enumerates tool-call workflows and diverse (benign/ambiguous) user scenarios to find residual unsafe interaction patterns missed by existing benchmarks.
rationale: Benign or ambiguous users; harm from tool-call reasoning failures, explicitly not adversarial.

title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'LLM agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks, where malicious tasks embedded in tool-retrieved information can redirect the agent to take unauthorized actions... We present MELON..., a novel IPI defense.' MELON detects attacks by re-executing the agent's trajectory with a masked user prompt and comparing tool calls.
rationale: Defense against indirect prompt injection on AgentDojo.

title: AgentSight: System-Level Observability for AI Agents Using eBPF
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: Case Study 2 (Reasoning Loop Detection): a research agent 'repeatedly called a web search tool with incorrect arguments, received an error, but then failed to correct its mistake, retrying the exact same failing command. AgentSight's real-time monitors detect this anomalous resource consumption... The LLM identified the root cause as a persistent tool error, noting the agent was caught in a "try-fail-re-reason" loop.' No adversary involved, purely a tool-usage/error failure. | ADV: Case Study 1 (Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks): 'a software development agent is instructed to clone and build a C project. The project's README file directed the agent to a URL serving HTML with a hidden prompt. This prompt made the agent read and send /etc/passwd to a collection server... AgentSight captured the full correlated attack chain: from the initial URL fetch to the final network exfiltration... The observer LLM analyzed this trace, returned a high-confidence attack score.'
rationale: Both: one case study on an injection and exfiltration attack, another on a benign tool error causing a loop.

title: SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'a foreseeable issue is that those embodied agents can also flawlessly execute some hazardous tasks, potentially causing damages in the real world... rigorously curated to cover 10 potential hazards' (e.g., Fire Hazard, Spill Damage, Electrical Shock, Explosion, Poisoning) arising from the agent literally/naively executing user or self-generated instructions, with no adversarial party crafting the hazardous instructions.
rationale: Hazardous tasks executed through poor planning; jailbreaks appear only in related work.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'external content introduces the risk of indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks, where malicious instructions are embedded within the content processed by LLMs, aiming to manipulate these agents into executing detrimental actions against users... We evaluate 30 different LLM agents and show that agents are vulnerable to IPI attacks.'
rationale: Adversarial indirect prompt-injection benchmark (direct harm and exfiltration).

title: Guaranteed Safe Satellite Guidance and Navigation Using Reachability Based Switching Controllers
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'we consolidate these two goals by synthesizing a formally safe controller and a runtime assurance logic that can switch between the safety and experimental controllers to guarantee the safe operation of a satellite... We deploy the synthesized safety controller and switching logic in close-proximity scenarios with both static and dynamic obstacles and show that the satellite remains safe.' The threat model is disturbances/uncertainty and an unverified 'experimental' controller, not an adversary.
rationale: Runtime assurance for collision avoidance with an unverified controller; no adversary.

title: ICON: Indirect Prompt Injection Defense for Agents based on Inference-Time Correction
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'Large Language Model (LLM) agents are susceptible to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks, where malicious instructions in retrieved content hijack the agent's execution... We introduce a Latent Space Trace Prober to detect attacks... ICON achieves a competitive 0.4% ASR.'
rationale: Detection and mitigation of indirect prompt injection; explicit adversary in the threat model.

title: STAC: When Innocent Tools Form Dangerous Chains to Jailbreak LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'STAC chains together tool calls that each appear harmless in isolation but, when combined, collectively enable harmful operations that only become apparent at the final execution step... state-of-the-art LLM agents... are highly vulnerable to STAC, with attack success rates (ASR) exceeding 90%.'
rationale: Red-teaming of a multi-turn attack class against tool-enabled agents.

title: SafeScientist: Toward Risk-Aware Scientific Discoveries by LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: SciSafetyBench risk taxonomy includes non-adversarial hazard categories: 'The task has unintentional bad consequences - The user has no harmful intent, but the requested task may accidentally result in harm (like large-scale molecule replication)' and 'The task is intrinsically risky... execution process involves safety hazards.' The Tool-Use Monitor 'identifies unsafe usage of simulated scientific tools, avoiding misuse and potential risk regarding experimental tools' (e.g., lab equipment operated outside safe parameters), independent of any adversary. | ADV: 'we employ 7 query injection methods designed to obscure risky topics... Do Anything Now (DAN)... DeepInception (DI) leverages the personification capabilities of LLMs to construct a virtual nested scene, enabling them to bypass usage controls' and 'Prompt Monitor: We adopt LLaMA-Guard... to screen inputs and identify adversarial prompt injections,' evaluated against jailbreak/injection attack methods (Table 3).

title: SOTER: A Runtime Assurance Framework for Programming Safe Robotics Systems
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'an integrated runtime assurance (RTA) system that helps enable the use of uncertified components, while still providing safety guarantees... ensure the safety of the system, including when untrusted third-party components have bugs or deviate from the desired behavior.' The threat model concerns uncertified/buggy components and environmental dynamics, not deliberate manipulation.

title: ZT-ICAS: A Zero-Trust Integrity-Constrained Framework for Agentic Vulnerability Scanning
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'embedding agentic reasoning into security workflows fundamentally expands the attack surface, as these systems must ingest adversarially controllable inputs... This exposure allows attackers to exploit the scanner via prompt injection and reasoning manipulation... We propose a Zero-Trust architecture enforcing semantic input neutralization, ephemeral context sharding, and capability-bounded tool invocation.'
rationale: Zero-trust layers evaluated against injection, context poisoning and RCE campaigns.

title: Taxonomy, Evaluation and Exploitation of IPI-Centric LLM Agent Defense Frameworks
evidence_excerpt: ADV: 'Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents with function-calling capabilities are increasingly deployed, but remain vulnerable to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks that hijack their tool calls... we design three novel adaptive attacks that significantly improve attack success rates targeting specific frameworks.'
rationale: Taxonomy, benchmarking and bypass of injection defenses with an explicit adversary.

title: Nuclear Deployed: Analyzing Catastrophic Risks in Decision-making of Autonomous LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'LLM agents can autonomously engage in catastrophic behaviors and deception, without being deliberately induced... such risks can originate from trade-offs between the agent's Helpful, Harmlessness and Honest (HHH) goals... we empirically prove the existence of catastrophic risks in autonomous LLM agents.' The risk arises from emergent goal trade-offs under stress, not from an adversary manipulating the agent.
rationale: Explicitly excludes attacks: studies the agent's own catastrophic decisions under stress.

title: CRALA: A Chinese-centric Risk Simulation and Assessment Framework for LLM Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'if a user says in Chinese "Delete file and release disk" (which means "delete files to free up disk space"), an LLM agent might misunderstand and run a dangerous command like "sudo rm -rf /*" if it has root permission. This can cause very big data loss.' Example risky scenarios include misdiagnosis by an online doctor agent and inappropriate scheduling -- all arising from misunderstanding benign instructions, with no adversary in the threat model.
rationale: Agents misunderstand benign instructions and cause accidental harm; no adversary.

title: Conformal Predictive Monitoring for Multi-Modal Scenarios
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'we consider an autonomous vehicle approaching an intersection. The vehicle might turn left, turn right, or go straight — each representing a distinct mode... the latter mode violates safety/traffic rules.' The method (GenQPM) provides statistically-guaranteed prediction intervals for STL robustness under stochastic, multi-modal environmental dynamics (e.g., unpredictable pedestrians/vehicles), with no adversary.
rationale: Predictive monitoring under stochastic environment dynamics; no adversary.

title: Evaluating Cultural and Social Awareness of LLM Web Agents
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'LLM agents demonstrate significantly better cultural and social awareness in non-agent environments compared to web-based agent environments, with agents achieving less than 10% awareness coverage and over 40% violation rates' when facing culturally/socially sensitive queries or 'misleading web content' (e.g., synthetic product listings). The failure mode is the agent's own capability gap (lack of cultural/social awareness) causing socially harmful autonomous actions, not a deliberately crafted adversarial attack.
rationale: Agents fail to recognize norm-violating content in synthetic sites; no attacker.

title: The Importance of Safety Invariants in Robustness Testing Autonomy Systems
evidence_excerpt: FUNC: 'robustness testing must involve invariant checking of safety properties to be effective, because passing unit tests and the absence of software crashes do not make a sufficient safety case... a large proportion of bugs found in mature systems would not have been discovered without invariant checking... represent physical safety violations of the systems' (e.g., speed-limit violations, self-collision). The threat model is faults/errors/unexpected inputs during robustness testing, with no adversary.
rationale: Fault and robustness testing revealing physical safety violations; no adversary.
